# Every-dimensional affine-frustum lower pointwise dual

This proves the lower half of the centered-layer common-c ansatz for all affine frusta in every continuous dimension d>=2. The upper half remains a separate obligation. In particular this is not a proof of the mixed-integer conjecture.

Dependencies are the exact physical records in `candidate 0ab50bc17861492a`, the proved cone-energy bounds in `candidate 6146c77d1d7c5e08`, and the constants lemma `candidate ff46898305c5fc7e`. The last lemma has been independently checked here: its monotone density quantile argument, decreasing tilt, and full-section identity give exactly (2) below.

## 1. Statement and notation

Write a=1/(H+1), p=(1-a)^d, and assume 0<a<1/d. This is the branch with a unique positive individually centered cone slope s*>1. Put

    v*=(s*+1)/(2s*),  e*=C(s*)/C(0),  R=1+a s*,
    t(T)=p(1+aT)^(-d),  t*=t(s*),
    kappa(T)=(v*+t(T))/(1+e*).

For s<=1 let v(s)=1; for s>=1 let v(s)=(s+1)/(2s). The cone coarea ratio is

    e(s)=(1/(2s)) int_-s^min(s,1) (1-ab)^(-d) db,

with its continuous value e(0)=1. Then for EVERY T>=s* and EVERY 0<=s<=T,

    1-v(s)-kappa(T)(1-e(s)) >=0.                    (1)

This is pointwise in the slope: no mixture centering is used in (1).

For orientation, the corrected normalized frustum cap record is

    F(s)=kappa(T)e(s)+1-v(s)-t(T).

Its desired lower value is kappa(T)-t(T), and their difference is precisely (1). Dividing by 1-t(T) gives the ansatz constant beta(T) of the constants lemma.

We use the already proved facts

    2v*-1 <= e* <= v* <=1,
    2p <=1+t*,
    2v*-1=2p e*-t*,
    beta(t*)=(v*-t*e*)/[(1-t*)(1+e*)] <=1/2.       (2)

The last three follow from the actual centered full section at cutoff T=s*, not an unproved functional inequality.

## 2. Reduction to one endpoint

For s<=1, Jensen applied to the even uniform base layer gives e(s)>=1, so (1) is immediate. It is also immediate for any s>=1 having e(s)>=1. Suppose s>1 and e(s)<1. Set

    J(s)=int_-s^1(1-ab)^(-d)db
        =[(1-a)^(1-d)-(1+as)^(1-d)]/[a(d-1)],
    Rratio(s)=(1-v(s))/(1-e(s))=(s-1)/(2s-J(s)).

The function J is strictly concave and J(1)>2. Wherever the denominator is positive,

    Rratio'(s)=[2-J(s)+(s-1)J'(s)]/[2s-J(s)]^2 <0, (3)

because J(s)-J(1)>= (s-1)J'(s). Also 2s-J(s) is convex, is negative at s=1, and tends to infinity; hence its positive set in (1,infinity) is an interval extending to infinity. Thus it is enough to prove

    Rratio(T)>=kappa(T)                            (4)

whenever e(T)<1. We prove its cross-multiplied form for every T>=s*, so no denominator exception remains.

## 3. Endpoint numerator and its curvature

Define

    E(T)=2T[(1+e*)(1-v(T))-(v*+t(T))(1-e(T))]
        =A T-(1+e*)+(v*+t(T))J(T)-2Tt(T),
    A=1+e*-2v* >=0.

Put q=1+aT and N(q)=a E((q-1)/a). Direct substitution gives

    N(q)=Aq+constant+Bq^(-d)-Cq^(1-d)-Dq^(1-2d),  (5)
    B=(1-a)/(d-1)+2p,
    C=2p+v*/(d-1),
    D=p/(d-1).

The omitted constant is -A-a(1+e*)+v*(1-a)^(1-d)/(d-1); its value does not enter derivatives. Thus

    q^(2d+1)N''(q)/d
       =G(q):=(d+1)B q^(d-1)-(d-1)C q^d-2(2d-1)D.

Moreover

    G'(q)=(d-1)q^(d-2)[(d+1)B-dCq].               (6)

Consequently G first increases and then decreases on the positive axis. We next show G(1)>=0. With r=1-a in ((d-1)/d,1),

    G(1)=[(d+1)r-2r^d]/(d-1)-v* >=1-v* >=0.     (7)

Indeed f(r)=(d+1)r-2r^d is concave. At r=1 it equals d-1. At r=(d-1)/d its excess over d-1 is r[1-2r^(d-1)]>=0, since

    (1+1/(d-1))^(d-1)>=2

by the binomial theorem. Concavity proves (7) throughout the interval.

It follows from (6)-(7) and G(q)->-infinity that on [1,infinity), N'' is nonnegative and then nonpositive, with either initial interval permitted to be empty. In particular, on every [R,infinity), the function N' has NO interior minimum; its lower bound is the smaller of N'(R) and its limit at infinity.

## 4. Both endpoint derivatives are nonnegative

Equation (5) gives N'(infinity)=A>=0. Because N'(R)=E'(s*), differentiating the exact expression for E and using J'(s*)=t*/p gives

    E'(s*)=A+(v*+t*)t*/p-2t*+2s*t'(s*)(e*-1).

The centered-section identity in (2) factors the first three terms EXACTLY:

    A+(v*+t*)t*/p-2t*
        =(1+t*-2p)[e*+t*/(2p)].                  (8)

Every term on the right is nonnegative. Also t'(s*)<0 and e*-1<=0, so

    N'(R)=E'(s*)>=0.

The no-interior-minimum conclusion of Section3 now gives N'(q)>=0 for every q>=R.

Finally E(s*)>=0 is equivalent, after multiplying positive denominators, to beta(t*)<=1/2 from (2). Hence N(R)>=0. Since N is nondecreasing on [R,infinity), N(q)>=0 there. Returning to T proves the cross-multiplied inequality (4), and Sections1-2 prove (1) for all s<=T.

All inequalities are exact in d. The proof permits boundary equality e(T)=1 directly through the cross-multiplied expression. The records at s=0 are continuous; the compactified slope infinity is handled separately by its corrected cap value V/2. Constant affine profiles and branches with no positive centered cone layer have the direct one-sign treatment already recorded in the planar-frustum note; no part of their argument depends on d=2.

# Every-dimensional affine-frustum lower pointwise dual

**All-dimensional lower pointwise frustum dual**

For d>=2 and 0<a<1/d, let s*>1 be the unique positive centered cone slope from the source's cone-moment equation. Put v(s)=1 for 0<=s<=1 and v(s)=(s+1)/(2s) for s>=1. For s>0 define e(s)=(2s)^(-1) integral_(-s)^(min(s,1)) (1-a b)^(-d) db, and set e(0)=1 by continuous extension. Put p=(1-a)^d and kappa(T)=[v(s*)+p(1+aT)^(-d)]/[1+e(s*)]. Then 1-v(s)-kappa(T)(1-e(s))>=0 for every T>=s* and 0<=s<=T. This is only the lower pointwise dual; it does not prove the corresponding all-dimensional upper dual or the full frustum two-law inequality.

Scope limits: Only the lower half of the common-c frustum ansatz is certified here. The corresponding all-dimensional upper dual is a separate obligation; no mixture centering is needed for this lower inequality.
